question: Which institution played a key role in influencing the structural reforms of the industrial sector in India post 1991?
solution: The correct answer is __**IMF and World Bank**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** • **IMF** (International Monetary Fund) and **World Bank** played a pivotal role in guiding India’s structural reforms post the **1991 economic crisis**. • India faced a **balance of payments crisis** in 1991, compelling the government to approach the IMF and World Bank for financial assistance. • In return for financial aid, these institutions recommended the implementation of structural reforms, which included **liberalization, privatization, and globalization** (LPG). • The reforms focused on reducing government control over industries, eliminating unnecessary regulatory barriers, and encouraging private sector participation in the economy. • IMF and World Bank encouraged India to adopt measures such as **foreign direct investment (FDI), reduction of tariffs**, and **currency devaluation** to improve economic stability and growth.
